title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 2 of these notes ("Structures de carré combinatoire") sets up the combinatorial notion of a square, i.e. a 4-gon, in several equivalent ways. The point is to be able to transport structures canonically between them. On the previous page Grothendieck is working with S_I for a 4-element set I, its Klein subgroup V, the three Sylow 2-subgroups (dihedral of order 8) and the cyclic subgroups of order 4.

The three descriptions given here:
(1) An incidence system (S, A, R): a set of vertices S, a set of edges A, and an incidence relation R ⊂ S×A, satisfying the usual polygon axioms (|S| = |A| = 4, each vertex on 2 edges, each edge has 2 vertices, the incidence graph is connected, i.e. an 8-cycle). The fixed-point-free 'antipodal' involution a acts on S and on A.
(2) A degree-2 map S → D with D = S/a, the set of the two diagonals. Equivalently, a partition of the 4-element set S into two 2-element subsets.
(3) A degree-2 map A → C with C = A/a, the set of the two codiagonals (pairs of opposite edges). Equivalently, a partition of the 4-element set A into two pairs.

He remarks that (1) is autodual (it exchanges vertices and edges symmetrically), while (2) privileges vertices and (3) privileges edges.

The next page completes the picture:
- It adds (2bis) and (3bis): S, resp. A, as a torsor under a group Γ that is a 'form' of Z/4Z, i.e. a cyclic orientation.
- It gives the explicit passages. From (2) to (1): A = P_2(S) minus the two diagonals, which is 4 of the 6 pairs, with tautological incidence. From (1) to the torsor descriptions: D = Aut(Q), dihedral of order 8, with its Klein subgroups V_S and V_A.

In modern terms, a square structure on a 4-element set S is the same as one of its 3 pair-partitions. Equivalently, it is a choice of one of the three dihedral Sylow 2-subgroups of S_S, or of a nonzero element of V. This is the bookkeeping behind the elliptic-curve context: the 4 branch points of E → P^1 in characteristic ≠ 2 have pair-partitions corresponding to nonzero 2-torsion points. Combined with cyclic orientations, this presumably feeds into level-2/level-4 type structures and the S_4 ≅ PGL_2(F_3)-type symmetries studied in the dossier.
errors: No mathematical errors. Note: description (2) as written ('a family of two sets of cardinal 2') still requires the two pairs to be disjoint and cover S, i.e. S → D of degree 2. This is implicit in the diagram.

ideas.what: Equivalent descriptions of a combinatorial square: incidence system (S,A,R); partition of vertices into two diagonals; partition of edges into two pairs of opposite edges; later, torsor under a form of Z/4
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of groupoids of 4-gon structures; square structure ↔ pair-partition of a 4-set ↔ Sylow 2-subgroup (D_4) of S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / elementary combinatorics and group theory
ideas.where_published: Similar 'cartographic'/combinatorial polygon structures appear in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (maps, dessins), but this specific treatment is unsure

ideas.what: Autoduality of the incidence description versus the vertex-biased and edge-biased descriptions
ideas.modern_name: Vertex–edge duality of polygons (self-dual regular polygon)

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, careful combinatorial set-up (equivalent descriptions of a square structure on a 4-set) serving as bookkeeping for symmetries of 2- and 4-torsion data of elliptic curves. Nothing new or uncredited on this page.
